temperature.

stem.text:
Solve\, algebraically.

$   "" _(n + 1 ) P _(2 )= 6   $

extensions.latexSource:
Solve, algebraically.

\[ { }_{n+1} P_{2}=6 \]

solution.text:
Using the permutation formula,

$ frac((n+1)!, (n-1)!) &= 6 \
  frac((n+1)n(n-1)!, (n-1)!) &= 6 \
  n(n+1) &= 6 \
  n^2+n-6 &= 0 \
  (n+3)(n-2) &= 0 $

The algebraic roots are $n=-3$ and $n=2$. Reject $n=-3$: the number of objects must allow a selection of two, so $n+1>=2$.

Therefore $n=2$. Check: $3 times 2=6$.

Scoring: $frac(1,2)$ mark for substitution; 1 mark for factorial expansion; $frac(1,2)$ mark for simplification; $frac(1,2)$ mark for the permissible value; $frac(1,2)$ mark for rejecting the extraneous root.

extensions.latexSource: \[ \begin{array}{rlrl} \frac{(n+1)!}{(n+1-2)!} & =6 & & 1 / 2 \text { mark for substitution } \\ \frac{(n+1)!}{(n-1)!} & =6 & & \\ \frac{(n+1)(n)(n-1)!}{(n-1)!} & =6 & & \begin{array}{l} 1 \text { mark for factorial expansion } \\ 1 / 2 \text { mark for simplification of factorials } \end{array} \\ n^{2}+n=6 & & \\ n^{2}+n-6=0 & & \\ (n+3)(n-2)=0 & & 1 / 2 \text { mark for the permissible value of } n \\ n=2 \text { mark for showing the rejection of the extraneous root } \\ & & 3 \text { marks } \end{array} \]
